extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in algebraic topology (learning fundamental group and van Kampen theorem)
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and conditions for computing fundamental groups (π1) of spaces: induced homomorphisms, product spaces, retracts, homotopy invariance, free products, and the van Kampen theorem with examples (wedges, graphs, knot complements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product space fundamental group
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are path-connected then π1(X × Y, (x0,y0)) ≈ π1(X,x0) × π1(Y,y0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A loop f in X×Y based at (x0,y0) corresponds to a pair of loops g in X and h in Y based at x0 and y0; homotopies correspond pairwise, giving a bijection [f] ↦ ([g],[h]) which is a group isomorphism. Example: π1(S1 × S1) ≈ Z × Z (torus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphism from a basepoint-preserving map
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ϕ:(X,x0)→(Y,y0), ϕ induces ϕ_*: π1(X,x0) → π1(Y,y0) defined by ϕ_*[f] = [ϕ ∘ f].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-defined because composing a homotopy of loops with ϕ yields a homotopy; ϕ_* is a group homomorphism since ϕ(f g) = (ϕf)(ϕg) (with the usual concatenation parametrization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of induced homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: (ϕψ)_* = ϕ_* ψ_* for compositions and (identity)_* = identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from associativity of composition of maps; hence fundamental group is a functor from based spaces and basepoint-preserving maps to groups and homomorphisms. In particular, a homeomorphism induces an isomorphism on π1 (inverse induces inverse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for factorizing loops via open cover (Lemma 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is the union of a collection of path-connected open sets Aα each containing the basepoint x0, and each intersection Aα ∩ Aβ is path-connected, then every loop in X at x0 is homotopic to a product of loops each of which is contained in a single Aα.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses compactness of I to partition domain so each subinterval maps into a single Aα, then inserts connecting paths gi in Ai ∩ Ai+1 from x0 to the partition points to express the loop as a concatenation of loops in the individual sets. This lemma provides the surjectivity ingredient for van Kampen.

rubrics_metrics.name: van Kampen theorem (existence and kernel description) (Theorem 1.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is the union of path-connected open sets Aα each containing basepoint x0 and each twofold intersection Aα ∩ Aβ is path-connected, then the natural homomorphism Φ: *α π1(Aα) → π1(X) is surjective. If additionally each triple intersection Aα ∩ Aβ ∩ Aγ is path-connected, then the kernel of Φ is the normal subgroup N generated by elements iαβ(ω) iβα(ω)^{-1} for ω ∈ π1(Aα ∩ Aβ), and hence π1(X) ≈ (*α π1(Aα)) / N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical procedure: cover X by appropriate open sets containing the basepoint and with connected intersections, compute π1 of each piece, form free product, then quotient by relations coming from inclusions of intersections. Proof uses factorizations of loops and rectangulation/homotopy arguments. Special-case (two sets) commonly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of intersection connectedness hypotheses for van Kampen
rubrics_metrics.description: Twofold intersections must be path-connected for Φ to be surjective; triple intersections must be path-connected for the kernel description to hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterexamples: S1 as union of two open arcs (twofold intersections disconnected → Φ not surjective); suspension of three points with cover by complements of points (triple intersection disconnected) yields incorrect result if triple-intersection hypothesis dropped — abelianization mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedge-sum application conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For wedge sum W = ∨α Xα (basepoints identified), if each basepoint xα is a deformation retract of an open neighborhood Uα in Xα, then π1(W) ≈ *α π1(Xα).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct open neighborhoods Aα = Xα ∪ ⋃_{β≠α} Uβ which deformation retract to Xα and have contractible intersections; apply van Kampen to conclude free-product decomposition. In particular π1(∨ of circles) is a free group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and deformation retraction consequences on π1 (Proposition 1.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X retracts onto subspace A, inclusion i_*: π1(A,x0) → π1(X,x0) is injective. If A is a deformation retract of X then i_* is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If r:X→A is a retraction then r i = identity so r_* i_* = identity_* implying injectivity; deformation retraction gives a homotopy pushing loops into A, showing surjectivity as well. Use to detect impossibility of retractions (e.g., S1 not a retract of D2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy invariance of induced maps (basepoint-fixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ_t : (X,x0) → (Y,y0) is a basepoint-preserving homotopy then ϕ0_* = ϕ1_*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composing a homotopy of maps with loops gives a homotopy of induced loops; hence homotopic basepoint-preserving maps induce the same homomorphism on π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation for non-basepoint-preserving homotopies (Lemma 1.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ_t : X → Y is a homotopy and h is the path t ↦ ϕ_t(x0) from ϕ0(x0) to ϕ1(x0), then ϕ0_* = β_h ϕ1_*, where β_h is the change-of-basepoint isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct partial paths ht and use concatenation to build homotopies of loops; this formula explains the conjugation/change-of-basepoint effect when homotopies move the basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalence implies π1-isomorphism (Proposition 1.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ:X→Y is a homotopy equivalence, then for any x0∈X the induced map ϕ_*: π1(X,x0) → π1(Y,ϕ(x0)) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a homotopy inverse ψ and Lemma 1.19 to see compositions are isomorphisms up to change-of-basepoint conjugation; deduce injectivity and surjectivity of ϕ_*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of simple-connectedness (Exercise 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a space X, the following are equivalent: (a) every map S1→X is homotopic to a constant map; (b) every map S1→X extends to a map D2→X; (c) π1(X,x0)=0 for all x0∈X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalences give practical alternative tests for simple-connectedness: extendability of loops to disks and nullhomotopy of circle-maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free product construction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The free product *α Gα consists of reduced words g1 g2 ... gm with letters gi ∈ G_{α_i} and adjacent letters from distinct factors; multiplication is concatenation followed by reduction (combine adjacent letters in same factor, cancel identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced words are unique representatives; associativity is established via permutation action on the set of reduced words. Universal property: any collection of homomorphisms ϕα: Gα → H extends uniquely to ϕ: *α Gα → H by ϕ(g1...gn) = ϕ_{α1}(g1)...ϕ_{αn}(gn). Use when van Kampen outputs free products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental group of a connected graph is free (graph + maximal tree construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a connected 1-dimensional CW complex (graph) X with maximal tree T, π1(X) is free on one generator for each edge not in T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose for each edge eα ∉ T a neighborhood retracting to T ∪ eα; intersections are contractible so van Kampen yields free product of circles. Generators can be explicit loops traveling in T to one end of eα, across eα, then back along T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of deformation retractions to compute complements of knots/links
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute π1(R3 − K) by showing R3 − K deformation retracts onto a simpler subcomplex (e.g., S1 ∨ S2, wedge sums, torus), then apply van Kampen or known π1 of the retract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: complement of one circle deformation retracts to S1 ∨ S2 so π1 ≈ Z; two unlinked circles retract to S1 ∨ S1 ∨ S2 ∨ S2 giving π1 ≈ Z * Z; two linked circles retract to S2 ∨ (S1×S1) yielding π1 ≈ π1(S1×S1) ≈ Z × Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding condition for torus knots (Example 1.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: For f(z) = (z^m, z^n): S1 → S1 × S1 ⊂ R3 to be an embedding representing a single knot Km,n, m and n must be relatively prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gcd(m,n)=d>1 then f is d-to-1 and the image is the knot K_{m/d, n/d}; signs of m or n change orientation (mirror image). The computation of π1 of the complement proceeds by realizing the complement deformation retracts onto a 2-complex built from mapping cylinders and applying van Kampen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change-of-basepoint homomorphism dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: The change-of-basepoint homomorphism β_h depends only on the homotopy class of the path h (Exercise 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact ensures well-definedness of conjugation relations when relating induced maps that move the basepoint; relates to condition in exercises about when π1(X) is abelian (basepoint-change depends only on endpoints).
